name: Pirelli HangarBicocca
funding: Founded and supported by Pirelli, its only named backer; Marco Tronchetti Provera chairs it. Technical sponsors include K-Way and M&C Saatchi Milano.
watch: Corporate Underwritten: Industrial contemporary space in Milan featuring Anselm Kiefer's 'The Seven Heavenly Palaces'. Provides free admission; governance is closely tied to Pirelli's corporate sponsorship and executive board oversight.
why_flagged: On 4 June 2026 Grizzly Research alleged Pirelli's Russian plants serve Rostec, a sanctioned group owning 25% of Pirelli Tyre Russia. Pirelli denies it.
records_note: No annual report or accounts; the about page names Pirelli as founder, three technical sponsors, and a board with chairman Marco Tronchetti Provera, undated.

name: Walker Art Center
funding: Principal, US Bank, Best Buy, Cargill Foundation, 3M.
records_note: It posts annual reports for 2010-11 to 2024-25 with audited statements for 2024-25, names corporate supporters by tier undated, and lists its trustees.

name: MAC Montréal
funding: Quebec crown corporation (C$12.5M Quebec grants, 2024-25). Donors: Banque Nationale (lead), Bronfman foundation, Power Corporation, AtkinsRéalis, BMO, RBC, Scotiabank, Desjardins.
watch: AtkinsRéalis (ex SNC-Lavalin) paid C$280M after its Libya fraud guilty plea in 2019. Loto-Québec, named earlier, is not in the 2024-25 report.
records_note: Publishes annual reports back to 2004-05; the 2024-25 report carries audited statements, thanks donors by name and lists the board as of 31 March 2025.

name: PHI Foundation
funding: Greenberg family (Minto real estate fortune). Federal and Quebec governments committed C$26.6M in 2022 for the PHI contemporain expansion. Programming is free.
watch: Contemporary art foundation in Old Montreal offering free public exhibitions.
records_note: Publishes no annual report, accounts or board list; the Partners Circle page shows six undated corporate logos, launched in 2025.

name: Lenbachhaus
funding: City of Munich gallery. On 18 September 2025 the council accepted gifts from Beisheim Stiftung, Pro Helvetia, Art Mentor Foundation Lucerne and Herbert Schuchardt-Stiftung.
watch: Operated by the City of Munich as a municipal cultural institution.
records_note: A Munich city gallery with no report or board of its own; the city posts consolidated accounts, and the gallery names six foundations, undated.

name: Benesse Art Site Naoshima
funding: Built by the Benesse Foundation, funded by Benesse Corporation (Fukutake family). EFU Investments and a BPEA EQT fund bought 70.1% of Benesse in March 2024.
watch: Cultural revitalization initiative across Naoshima, Teshima, and Inujima founded by Soichiro Fukutake.
records_note: The Fukutake Foundation, which runs the art, lists yearly plans and reports from FY2007 and a dated board; no donor list is published.

name: Ogden Museum
funding: Founder Roger Ogden's initial gift of about 600 works. The Helis Foundation funds free Thursday admission for Louisiana residents and presents the Poydras Corridor sculpture exhibition.
watch: The Helis family fortune came from oil. Its foundation currently pays for free Thursdays and the Poydras Corridor exhibition.
records_note: Names its trustees as of March 2026 but publishes no donor list, annual report or accounts; Form 990s for 2003 to 2025 sit on ProPublica.

name: Storm King Art Center
why_flagged: Bloomberg Philanthropies is listed in Storm King's 2025 donor list in the Ambassador tier ($100,000+).
records_note: It posts an income statement and balance sheet on its leadership page, names 2025 donors by tier, and lists its trustees, but no annual reports.

name: Artists Space
funding: NYSCA and NYC Cultural Affairs; Lambent, Mellon, Goldsmith, Keith Haring, Frankenthaler and Niarchos foundations. Core contributors include the I.A. O'Shaughnessy Foundation, named for oilman Ignatius O'Shaughnessy.
watch: Historic Tribeca alternative space founded in 1972. Famed for artist advocacy and institutional critique; operates with complete transparency and rejects corporate corporate board influence.
why_flagged: NYSCA and NYC Cultural Affairs; Lambent, Mellon, Goldsmith, Keith Haring, Frankenthaler and Niarchos foundations. Core contributors include the I.A. O'Shaughnessy Foundation, named for oilman Ignatius O'Shaughnessy.
records_note: Names core contributors and campaign donors with no date and lists its board; no annual report posted, Form 990s for 2001 to 2025 on ProPublica.

name: Noguchi Museum
records_note: Names its trustees and posts dated benefit donor listings; direct reads were blocked, so only ProPublica filings for 2003 to 2025 were opened.

name: Queens Museum
funding: City-owned building. Public funds from NYC Department of Cultural Affairs, NY State Council on the Arts, the state legislature, the Queens Borough President and City Council; foundations and members.
watch: In 2017 the museum cancelled, then reinstated, an Israeli UN event after backlash. In October 2023 staff sent a letter and struck over Palestine.
records_note: Names its public funders with no date and lists its trustees; no annual report on the site, Form 990s for 2001 to 2025 on ProPublica.

name: SculptureCenter
funding: Expenses $2.6M (FY2025). Teiger, Kellen, Warhol, Lambent, Hartwig, Woodner and Frankenthaler funds; NYSCA and NYC Cultural Affairs; an international council of collectors.
watch: Arison Arts Foundation and David Rockefeller Fund give through a New York arts network. No flagged funder, protest or censorship found.
records_note: No annual reports found; 990s are on ProPublica, the support page names donors without a date, and the board is listed.
